comment: Hand-written descriptions of what the platform offers. tools/build-index.mjs joins each entry with the examples that use it (detected from their code) and refuses to build if a pointer names a file missing from the pinned repository.

capabilities.title: Passkey sign-in (Memphis)
capabilities.summary: People sign in with a passkey on their device, or approve a computer from their phone. A contract learns who is calling from a Memphis session; no passwords and no wallets.
capabilities.frontend: @thebes/sdk MemphisGate, useMemphis; runtime passkey.js and memphis-connect.js

capabilities.title: HTTP outcalls
capabilities.summary: A contract fetches a URL from the open internet; the validator set agrees on the response and it is carried in a finalized block.
rules: Never put a secret (API key, token, password) in an outcall request's URL, headers or body. Call an authenticated API through your own service.

capabilities.title: On-chain randomness
capabilities.summary: raw_rand returns bytes no single validator can predict or choose, for shuffles, draws and identifiers.

capabilities.title: Images and files on chain
capabilities.summary: Upload images and files to a media contract and serve them by URL.

capabilities.title: Invoices and settlement
capabilities.summary: Invoices with partial payments that never overshoot; the settling payment marks the invoice paid in the same call.

capabilities.title: Owners, admins and users
capabilities.summary: An owner and admins per contract, user profiles, and paged reads that stay inside one reply.

capabilities.title: Upgrades that keep the data
capabilities.summary: Ship a new version of a contract to the same id and keep its state. The build must use moc --legacy-persistence.
rules: Build every Motoko contract with moc --legacy-persistence, or let thebes-deploy build it from `source`.

capabilities.title: Deploying
capabilities.summary: Sign installs with your own key, or deploy with an API key charged to credits; every new developer starts with free credits.
